facts.fact: Eravi came to Kettamala twenty years ago at forty from a coast clinic; a tapper's widow sold him cheap Resin House poppy and willow bark, paid for in news of weather and sickness. Six years ago a big gentle-spoken guild man asked him to open the old slop-gate postern for one night; Eravi wrote Asha's death up as a bear and kept the key.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires his twenty-year trade and the six-year-old postern unlocking.

facts.fact: Eravi gave the guild three pieces of news since the wedding: the sword hilt toward Neela (seen while sitting by Devan's sickbed), the cart order overheard in the passage outside the sickroom, and the drained west stair lamps. He was told the lamps were only meant to frighten.
facts.why: needed because the beat lists what he passed on.

facts.fact: Devan holds Eravi in the gate chamber over the padippura, under Bhaskaran's man, writing a dated account for Rema.
facts.why: needed to dispose of the informant before the next chapter.

facts.fact: Bhaskaran is at Kettamala; his men under Vasu (mother keeps ducks at Kalladi) were left at the Resin House with Pavi, and Vasu is the rider who comes off the wood road at first grey.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Bhaskaran at the fort and his lads locked out.

facts.fact: Devan and Muthu agree he will ask Muthu straight in future and Muthu will say 'I can't' when he cannot answer.
facts.why: needed for the apology and Muthu accepting it.
